# AWS Transfer Family

Store Transfer Family configuration or run loopback SFTP servers backed by S3.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `transfer` |
| Signing name | `transfer` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2018-11-05` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Default transfer.servers=records persists configuration without listening. In listen mode ONLINE servers expose loopback SFTP addresses in resource inventory; stop, delete, reset and shutdown close sessions. See the [Transfer guide](../guides/transfer-records.md). |
| Selected operations | 17 of 71 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#aws-transfer-family) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Only explicit SFTP/PUBLIC and a finite fixed policy set; VPC/EFS/certificates/custom identity, logging, workflow/connector, IP/storage/protocol advanced options are excluded, even false/null/empty.
- PATH is the default; directory targets are checked against S3 at access time. Session policies, POSIX and advanced logical mapping options remain excluded.
- CF SshPublicKeys is excluded; independently imported public-key IDs survive updates and live-state compensation. CF banner removal is rejected; explicit empty clears it.
- No FTP/FTPS/AS2, EFS, VPC endpoints, custom identity providers, host-key import/rotation, workflows, connectors, CloudWatch session logs or transfer EventBridge events.
- Uploads have a TinyStack 32 MiB per-file limit; no append/resume, session policies, logical FILE mappings, overlapping mappings or username substitutions; security-policy names do not constrain SSH negotiation.
- S3 directory rename, overwriting rename, links and default SETSTAT are unsupported, matching AWS; ENABLE_NO_OP is not selected.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
